answers.q1: To pray, first perform ablution; once the prayer time has begun, face the qibla and make the intention. Begin with the opening takbir, then complete the standing, bowing, prostrations and sittings in order; in the final sitting recite at-Tahiyyat and end the prayer with the salam.
answers.q2: Deliberately eating or drinking, marital relations, smoking and nutritional injections break the fast. In disputed cases, the safest way is to consult a reliable fiqh source or a religious scholar.
answers.q3: Zakat is given to the poor, the needy, debtors, stranded travellers and the other groups listed in Surah at-Tawbah, verse 60. It is not given to one's parents, grandparents, children or grandchildren.
answers.q4: In ablution you make the intention, wash the hands, mouth, nose, face and arms, wipe the head, and complete it by washing the feet including the ankles.
answers.q5: Reading the Qur'an is an act of worship, and every letter is rewarded. Reading regularly and with understanding keeps the heart alive, brings peace and strengthens one's religious knowledge.
answers.q6: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was born in Makkah in 571 and was given prophethood at the age of 40. He conveyed Islam in the Meccan and Medinan periods and passed away in Madinah in 632.
answers.q7: For the full ritual bath (ghusl), make the intention, then rinse the mouth thoroughly, rinse and clean the nose, and wash the whole body so that no part remains dry.
answers.q8: Tahajjud is a voluntary prayer of two to eight rak'ahs offered at night after Isha, after sleeping and waking. Praying it in the last third of the night is especially virtuous.
answers.q9: Missed obligatory prayers are made up with the intention of qada. For example: "I intend to make up the fard of the first Fajr prayer whose time I reached but did not pray." Only the fard prayers and witr are made up.
answers.q10: It is a corrective prostration made when a fard act is delayed or a wajib act is forgotten or delayed in the prayer. In the final sitting, after the Salli and Barik supplications, you give salam to the right and then make two prostrations.
answers.q11: Charity (sadaqah) is any material or spiritual help given for the sake of Allah. It averts hardship, cleanses sins, brings peace to the heart and strengthens mutual help in society.
answers.q12: Zakat al-fitr is a charity that is wajib for every Muslim who is able, in Ramadan. It is delivered to those in need before Eid al-Fitr, and may be given to anyone eligible for zakat.
answers.q13: A person who travels a distance regarded as a journey (about 90 km) and will stay less than 15 days at the destination counts as a traveller (in the Hanafi school). A traveller prays the four-rak'ah fard prayers as two.
answers.q14: They are prayers offered to draw closer to Allah beyond the fard and wajib. Duha, Tahajjud, Awwabin, Tahiyyat al-Masjid and the prayer of need are among the best known.
answers.q15: Repentance is regretting a sin and resolving never to repeat it. After sincerely asking for forgiveness, it is sunnah to pray two rak'ahs of repentance and to implore Allah.
answers.q16: On Laylat al-Qadr, which the Qur'an says is better than a thousand months, one should read much Qur'an, repent, pray qada and voluntary prayers, and make supplication.
answers.q17: Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime for every Muslim who is financially and physically able. It is performed by visiting the holy places in Makkah (the Kaaba, Arafat and others) on specific days.
answers.q18: Offering a sacrifice is a wajib act of worship (in the Hanafi school) for Muslims with a certain level of wealth. It is carried out by properly slaughtering a sacrificial animal for the sake of Allah during the days of Eid al-Adha.
answers.q19: Among the etiquettes of supplication: being in a state of ablution, facing the qibla, raising the hands, beginning and ending with praise of Allah and salawat, and asking sincerely while believing it will be answered.
answers.q20: Sunnah is the general name for the sayings, actions and tacit approvals of the Prophet (peace be upon him). A hadith is each oral or written report that conveys this sunnah to us.
answers.q21: Learning and memorising the beautiful names of Allah and turning to Him by these names in supplication brings relief to the heart, helps supplications be accepted and strengthens faith.
answers.q22: These are the rights people have over one another. They are not forgiven by Allah unless the wronged person forgives. To be free of them, find the person and seek their forgiveness; if they have died, pray for them.
answers.q23: Prayer in congregation is twenty-seven degrees more virtuous than praying alone. It strengthens unity, solidarity, mutual help and love among Muslims.
answers.q24: It means praying for the Prophet (peace be upon him) and asking peace for him (e.g. "Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad"). Allah has mercy on the one who sends salawat, and they attain the Prophet's intercession.
answers.q25: On the blessed nights it is recommended to fast during the day and, at night, to read the Qur'an, repent and seek forgiveness, pray qada and voluntary prayers, and send salawat upon the Prophet.

idgam_meal_gunne.title: Idgham Ma'al Ghunnah
idgam_meal_gunne.desc: It means reading with emphasis (shaddah) while making a nasal sound (ghunnah).
idgam_meal_gunne.rule: It occurs if one of the letters (ي م ن و) comes after Sakin Nun (نْ) or Tanween (ً ٍ ٌ).

0.explanation: The letter Nun merges into the letter Ya.

1.explanation: The letter Nun merges into the letter Mim.

idgam-bila-gunne.title: Idgham Bila Ghunnah
idgam-bila-gunne.desc: It means reading with emphasis (shaddah) without making a nasal sound (ghunnah).
idgam-bila-gunne.rule: It occurs if one of the letters (ل ر) comes after Sakin Nun or Tanween.

0.explanation: Nun is not pronounced, Ra is read with shaddah.

1.explanation: Tanween merges into the letter Lam.

ihfa.title: Ikhfa
ihfa.desc: If one of the Ikhfa letters comes after Sakin Nun or Tanween, the Nun sound is hidden and read with a nasal sound.
ihfa.rule: It occurs if one of the Ikhfa letters comes after Sakin Nun or Tanween.

1.explanation: The Nun sound is hidden while transitioning to the letter Shin.

izhar.title: Izhar
izhar.desc: If one of the throat letters comes after Sakin Nun or Tanween, the Nun sound is read clearly.
izhar.rule: It occurs if one of the throat letters comes after Sakin Nun or Tanween.

0.explanation: The Nun sound is pronounced clearly.

iklab.title: Iqlab
iklab.desc: If the letter Ba (ب) comes after Sakin Nun or Tanween, the Nun sound turns into the Mim (م) sound.
iklab.rule: It occurs if the letter Ba (ب) comes after Sakin Nun or Tanween.

kalkale.title: Qalqalah
kalkale.desc: When Qalqalah letters are calm (with sukoon), they are read with a vibration (echoing sound).
kalkale.rule: It occurs when Qalqalah letters are calm (with sukoon).

1.explanation: The letter Dal is vibrated at the end.

51.meaning: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Hell, from the punishment of the grave, from the trials of life and death, and from the evil of the trial of the False Messiah (Dajjal).

52.title: Goodness in Both Worlds
52.meaning: Our Lord. Give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter.

53.title: Increase in Knowledge
53.meaning: My Lord. Increase me in knowledge.

54.title: Forgiveness of Sins
54.meaning: Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs, make our feet firm, and help us against the disbelieving people.

55.title: Straight Path
55.meaning: Guide us to the straight path.

56.title: Mercy Prayer
56.meaning: My Lord. Have mercy on us.

57.title: Patience Prayer
57.meaning: Our Lord, pour patience upon us, make our feet firm, and help us against the disbelieving people.

58.title: Ease Not Difficulty
58.meaning: My Lord. Make it easy, not difficult.

60.title: Among Righteous
60.meaning: My Lord, inspire me to be grateful for the favour You have bestowed on me and on my parents, and to do righteous deeds that please You. And admit me by Your mercy among Your righteous servants.

61.title: Blessing Gratitude
61.meaning: My Lord. Inspire me to be grateful for Your blessings.

62.title: Hearing and Knowing
62.meaning: Our Lord. Accept from us. Indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing.

63.title: Pardon Prayer
63.meaning: O Allah. You are Pardoning and love to pardon, so pardon me.

64.title: Qunut Prayer
64.meaning: O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, grant me well-being among those You have granted well-being, take me into Your care among those You have taken into Your care, bless me in what You have given, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed. For You decree and none can decree over You. The one You befriend is never humiliated. Blessed and Exalted are You, our Lord.

65.title: Master of Forgiveness
65.meaning: O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no deity except You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I keep Your covenant and promise as best I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.

66.title: Travel Prayer
66.meaning: Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, for we could not have done so ourselves. And indeed, to our Lord we will return.

67.title: Meal Prayer
67.meaning: O Allah. Bless us in what You have provided.

68.title: Visiting the Sick
68.meaning: No harm, it will be a purification, if Allah wills.

69.title: Refuge from Satan
69.meaning: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.

70.title: Grave Torment Protection
70.meaning: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Hell, from the punishment of the grave, from the trials of life and death, and from the evil of the trial of the False Messiah (Dajjal).

71.title: Mosque Entry Prayer
71.meaning: O Allah. Open the gates of Your mercy for me.

72.title: Mosque Exit Prayer
72.meaning: O Allah. I ask You from Your bounty.

73.title: Post-Ablution Testimony
73.meaning: I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.

74.title: Funeral Prayer
74.meaning: O Allah, forgive him and have mercy on him, grant him well-being and pardon him. Make his reception honourable and his entrance spacious. Wash him with water, snow and hail, and cleanse him of sins as You cleanse a white garment of dirt. Give him a home better than his home, a family better than his family and a spouse better than his spouse. Admit him to Paradise and protect him from the punishment of the grave and the punishment of the Fire.

75.title: Seeking Mercy
75.meaning: O Allah. I ask You by Your mercy.

76.title: Friday Salawat
76.meaning: O Allah. Send blessings upon our master Muhammad.

77.title: Tasbeeh
77.meaning: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Allah.

78.title: Intercession Prayer
78.meaning: O Allah. Grant us the intercession of Your Prophet.

80.title: Night of Power Prayer
80.meaning: O Allah. You are Pardoning and love to pardon, so pardon me.

81.title: Reaching Ramadan
81.meaning: O Allah. Let us reach Ramadan.

82.title: Tawheed Dhikr
82.meaning: There is no deity except Allah, alone, without partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things.

83.title: Eid Takbir
83.meaning: Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. There is no deity except Allah. Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, and to Allah belongs all praise.

84.title: Talbiyah
84.meaning: Here I am, O Allah, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Surely all praise and blessings are Yours, and the dominion. You have no partner.

85.title: New Moon Prayer
85.meaning: O Allah, let this crescent rise over us with blessing and faith, with safety and Islam. (O crescent,) my Lord and your Lord is Allah.

86.title: Sha'ban Prayer
86.meaning: O Allah. Bless us in Sha'ban.

87.title: Blessed Days Prayer
87.meaning: O Allah. Make these days blessed for us.

90.title: Forgiveness and Mercy
90.meaning: My Lord, forgive me, have mercy on me, mend my shortcomings, provide for me and raise me in rank.

91.title: Confession of Wronging Oneself
91.meaning: O Allah, I have greatly wronged myself, and none forgives sins except You. So grant me forgiveness from Yourself and have mercy on me. Indeed, You are the Forgiving, the Merciful.

92.title: Adam's Repentance
92.meaning: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will surely be among the losers.

93.title: Best of Forgivers
93.meaning: My Lord. Forgive and have mercy. You are the best of those who show mercy.

94.title: Purification from Sins
94.meaning: O Allah, distance me from my sins as You have distanced the east from the west. O Allah, cleanse me of sins as a white garment is cleansed of dirt. O Allah, wash away my sins with water, snow and hail.

95.title: Living and Sustaining
95.meaning: I seek forgiveness from Allah, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer.

96.title: Pardoning and Generous
96.meaning: O Allah. You are Pardoning and Generous.

97.title: Forgetting and Mistakes
97.meaning: Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity. It will have the good it has earned and bear the evil it has earned. Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err. Our Lord, do not lay on us a burden like the one You laid on those before us. Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no strength to bear. Pardon us, forgive us and have mercy on us. You are our Protector, so help us against the disbelieving people.

98.title: Cleansing from Sins
98.meaning: O Allah. Cleanse me from sins.

101.title: Subhanaka
101.meaning: Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. Blessed is Your name and exalted is Your majesty, and there is no deity besides You.

102.title: Surah Al-Fatiha
102.meaning: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, Master of the Day of Judgement. You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help. Guide us to the straight path, the path of those You have blessed, not of those who have earned anger, nor of those who have gone astray.

103.title: Ruku Tasbeeh
103.meaning: Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent.

104.title: Sujood Tasbeeh
104.meaning: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.

105.title: Tahiyyat
105.meaning: All greetings, prayers and good words are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.

106.title: Allahumma Salli
106.meaning: O Allah. Send blessings upon Muhammad.

107.title: Allahumma Barik
107.meaning: O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.

108.title: Rabbana Prayer
108.meaning: Our Lord. Give us good in this world.

109.title: Salam
109.meaning: Peace and mercy of Allah be upon you.

110.title: Post-Salam Prayer
110.meaning: O Allah, You are Peace and from You is peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honour.

111.title: Qunut Prayer
111.meaning: O Allah, we seek Your help, Your forgiveness and Your guidance. We believe in You, turn to You in repentance and rely upon You. We praise You with all good. We thank You and are not ungrateful to You, and we abandon and forsake whoever disobeys You.

112.title: Prophet Yunus Prayer
112.meaning: There is no deity except You. Glory be to You. Indeed I have been of the wrongdoers.

113.title: Grief Prayer
113.meaning: O Allah. I am Your servant.

114.title: Sufficiency Verse
114.meaning: If they turn away, say: Allah is sufficient for me; there is no deity except Him. On Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.

115.title: Hope for Mercy
115.meaning: O Allah, it is Your mercy that I hope for, so do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye, and set right all my affairs. There is no deity except You.

116.title: Living and Sustaining
116.meaning: O Ever-Living, O Sustainer. I seek help through Your mercy.

117.title: Difficulty to Ease
117.meaning: O Allah. Nothing is easy except what You make easy.

118.title: Grief Protection
118.meaning: O Allah. I seek refuge in You from grief.

119.title: Calamity Prayer
119.meaning: Indeed, we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we will return. O Allah, reward me in my affliction and replace it for me with something better.

120.title: Rain of Patience
120.meaning: Our Lord. Pour upon us patience.

121.title: Allah is With Me
121.meaning: Allah is with me, Allah is watching over me.

122.title: Hope Verse
122.meaning: Do not despair of the mercy of Allah.

123.title: Tawakkul Verse
123.meaning: And upon Allah let the believers rely.

1.question: In the verse below, the letter 'ي' comes after 'ن'. Which tajweed rule applies?
1.explanation: Because one of the letters of idgham with ghunnah comes after sakin nun, idgham with ghunnah applies.

2.question: Which rule applies when no cause of madd comes after a letter of madd?

3.question: Which letters are qalqalah letters?
options: أ ه ع ح غ خ
3.explanation: The qalqalah letters are qaf, ta, ba, jim, and dal.

4.question: What happens if the letter 'ب' comes after sakin nun or tanwin?
4.explanation: Ba is the letter of iqlab, so the nun sound changes into a mim sound.

5.question: How many ikhfa letters are there?

6.question: When is the letter 'Ra' pronounced lightly?
options: When it has shadda with fatha
6.explanation: The letter Ra is pronounced lightly when it has kasra.

q1.question: In which year was the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) born?
q1.explanation: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was born in Makkah in 571 CE, about 50 days after the Event of the Elephant.

q2.question: Which is the longest surah in the Quran?
q2.explanation: Surah Al-Baqarah has 286 verses and is the longest surah in the Quran. It was revealed in Madinah.

q3.question: Which of the following is not one of the obligatory acts of wudu?
q3.explanation: Wudu has four obligatory acts: washing the face, washing the arms, wiping a quarter of the head, and washing the feet. Rinsing the mouth is sunnah.

q4.question: Who narrated the hadith "Actions are judged by intentions"?
q4.explanation: This hadith was narrated from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) and is the first hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari.

q5.question: Where was the first revelation sent down?
q5.explanation: The first revelation was brought by Jibril (peace be upon him) in the Cave of Hira in 610 CE. The first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq were revealed.

q6.question: How many juz does the Quran contain?
q6.explanation: The Quran consists of 30 juz. Each juz is about 20 pages, and reading one juz per day in Ramadan is a common practice.

q7.question: What is the surah recited after Al-Fatihah in prayer called?
q7.explanation: The short surah recited after Al-Fatihah is commonly called an additional surah. It is one of the required parts of prayer in many fiqh rulings.

q8.question: What was the name of the Prophet Muhammad's milk mother?
q8.explanation: According to tradition, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was nursed by Halimah as-Sa'diyyah and stayed with her for several years.

q9.question: Which surah is the only one that does not begin with the Basmala?
q9.explanation: Surah At-Tawbah is the only surah that does not begin with the Basmala. It contains strong warnings to those who opposed the Muslims.

q10.question: Who said, "Paradise lies beneath the feet of mothers"?
q10.explanation: This narration is attributed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and emphasizes the great status and rights of mothers.

q11.question: For whom is the Friday prayer obligatory?
q11.explanation: Friday prayer is obligatory for free, sane, adult, resident, and healthy men. It is not obligatory for women, travelers, or the sick.

q12.question: Who is the only woman mentioned by name in the Quran?
q12.explanation: Maryam is the only woman mentioned by name in the Quran. Her name appears many times, and Surah Maryam is named after her.

q13.question: What was the first qiblah of the Muslims?
q13.explanation: The first qiblah of the Muslims was Masjid al-Aqsa in Jerusalem. Later, the qiblah was changed to the Kaaba in Makkah.

q14.question: When is tayammum performed?
q14.explanation: Tayammum is performed with clean earth or stone when water is unavailable or cannot be used because of illness or similar reasons.

q15.question: How does the hadith continue: "Make things easy, do not make them difficult..."?
options: Do not frighten; give glad tidings
Smile; do not make people cry
Give glad tidings; do not repel people
q15.explanation: The full meaning is: "Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give glad tidings and do not repel people." It teaches gentleness in inviting people to faith.
